  The records available for West Bromwich, Staffordshire, from 1875 to 1905 are rich and largely accessible online. The town lies in the Black Country, in the ancient South Offlow Hundred of Staffordshire, and falls within the West Bromwich Civil Registration District (GRO, from 1837). Its Church of England parishes range from the ancient All Saints (registers from 1608) to newer Victorian churches like Holy Trinity and St John the Evangelist, and there is a Roman Catholic parish (St Michael and Holy Angels) with records from 1832. For the specific 1875–1905 window, civil registration is essentially complete (mandatory from 1875), the 1881, 1891, and 1901 census returns are fully indexed and free on FamilySearch, and dozens of parish baptism and marriage registers are name-indexed online. The most important caution is that All Saints Church's Bishop's Transcripts end around 1868, so christenings at that parish after that date require the Staffordshire Record Office originals or the FamilySearch church records collection 2364451. The 1911 census — which asked mothers to state how many children they had born alive and how many were still living — is also now fully online and should be consulted as a direct check on whether additional children existed.

Primary GRO civil registration indexes and census collections are accessible through FreeBMD (free), Staffordshire BMD (free), FamilySearch collections 2285338/2285732/2285341/1321821/1865747/1888129, Ancestry, and Findmypast as documented in the guide.

West Bromwich transferred to the metropolitan county of West Midlands (Sandwell) in 1974; for all genealogy research in this 1875–1905 period, search under Staffordshire. FamilySearch and record indexes use pre-1974 Staffordshire boundaries throughout.

Parish registers are filed by individual church, not by civil registration district — search all West Bromwich churches when a christening is not found in one register (All Saints, Christ Church, Holy Trinity, St John the Evangelist, St Paul, St Peter, St Andrew, plus nonconformist and Catholic chapels).

All Saints Church (C of E, the ancient parish) Bishop's Transcripts run only to 1868; for 1875–1905 christenings at All Saints, consult the original parish registers at the Staffordshire Record Office or verify coverage within FamilySearch collection 2364451 (England, Staffordshire, Church Records, 1538–1944).

St Michael and Holy Angels (Roman Catholic) was known as St Michael's before 1877; earlier records can be found at Walsall (per FamilySearch Catalog koha:762327). Catholic baptism volumes 1878–1933 are online but browse-only; marriages 1855–1947 are 73% name-indexed.

Civil registration before 1875 had up to 15% non-compliance nationally; from 1875 registration was mandatory with penalties. For the 1875–1905 target period, GRO index coverage should be essentially complete.

Cross-border: West Bromwich lies adjacent to the Walsall registration district (Staffordshire, also Hannah Earnest's native district of Darlaston), the Smethwick district, and is approximately 5 miles from Birmingham (Warwickshire). Check adjacent registration districts when a birth is not found in West Bromwich.

The 1911 census (now online: FamilySearch collection 1921547, Ancestry 2352) gives parents' own statement of the number of children born alive and number still living — use this to estimate whether births in the 1875–1905 window remain unaccounted for in the tree.
entry.guide_markdown:
# Locality Guide: West Bromwich, Staffordshire, England (1875–1905)

## Jurisdiction overview
- **Formed:** West Bromwich was a village before 1801 (historically written Bromwic, Bromwych, etc.); it became a town from 1801 and a Municipal Borough in 1882, elevated to County Borough status in 1889. The West Bromwich Civil Registration District was established 1 July 1837.
- **Administrative center:** West Bromwich town centre.
- **Parent jurisdiction:** Staffordshire (historically); transferred to the new metropolitan county of West Midlands (Sandwell Metropolitan Borough) in 1974.
- **Population during period:** A major Black Country industrial town. The 2021 Census recorded 103,112 residents (Wikipedia). It was already a densely populated manufacturing centre by 1875.
- **Economy:** Iron founding, coal mining, nail and tube making, hardware manufacture — the dominant Black Country trades.
- **Ethnic composition:** Predominantly English-born working class, with some Irish migration. Nonconformist denominations were strong.
- **Religious denominations:** Church of England — All Saints (ancient parish), Christ Church, Holy Trinity, St John the Evangelist, St Paul, St Peter, St Andrew; Roman Catholic — St Michael and Holy Angels (from 1832); Wesleyan Methodists (five meeting-houses); Independents (four); Baptists (two); Primitive Methodists and others. (Per [West Bromwich All Saints, Staffordshire, England Genealogy](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/West_Bromwich_All_Saints,_Staffordshire,_England_Genealogy))
- **Key historical events:** West Bromwich County Borough created 1882; Second Boer War 1899–1902 affected many families.

## Boundary changes
- West Bromwich was a Staffordshire town and Civil Registration District from 1837 to 1974; boundaries were stable throughout the 1875–1905 target period.
- In 1974 the Local Government Act transferred West Bromwich to West Midlands (Sandwell). FamilySearch and all genealogy tools index records under the pre-1974 Staffordshire label; search under Staffordshire for this entire period.
- The adjacent Walsall registration district (Staffordshire) includes Darlaston, birthplace of Hannah Earnest; the Birmingham registration district (Warwickshire) is approximately 5 miles away. Records for family members may appear in either adjacent district.

## Available record types

All civil registration in England operates at the **national (GRO) level** — births, marriages, and deaths were registered at local register offices and indexed quarterly by the General Register Office from 1 July 1837. There is no county- or town-level civil registration series separate from the GRO.

### Vital records (civil registration)
- **Start date:** National (GRO) level, 1 July 1837. Compliance was essentially universal from 1875, when registration became mandatory with financial penalties. Per [England Civil Registration](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/England_Civil_Registration).
- **What exists:** Births, marriages, and deaths for the West Bromwich Registration District, registered quarterly. Birth certificates give: birth date and place, child's name and sex, father's name and occupation, mother's full name including maiden name, informant's name and relationship, date registered.
- **Where held:** Free quarterly index at [FreeBMD](http://www.freebmd.org.uk/) (covers 1837–1983+) and at [GRO online search](https://www.gro.gov.uk/gro/content/certificates/indexes_search.asp). FamilySearch: [England and Wales Birth Registration Index, 1837–2008](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/2285338) (free, indexed). Ancestry: [England & Wales Civil Registration Birth Index, 1837–1915](https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/8912/) (subscription); [Staffordshire, England, Birth, Marriage and Death Indexes, 1837–2017](https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/staffordshirebmds/) (subscription). Local free index: [Staffordshire BMD](http://www.staffordshirebmd.org.uk/); [West Midlands BMD](http://www.westmidlandsbmd.org.uk/). Original certificates must be ordered from the GRO.
- **Gaps:** No significant gaps are indicated for the 1875–1905 period. Note: The GRO index entry alone does not give parents' names for pre-1911 births — order the certificate to obtain the mother's maiden name and informant.

### Church records
- **Denominations present:** Church of England: All Saints (ancient parish, registers from 1608, Bishop's Transcripts from 1676; chapelries St Paul 1853, St Peter 1858); Christ Church (registers from 1829); Holy Trinity (registers from 1841); St John the Evangelist (from 1879); St James (formerly Hill Top). Roman Catholic: St Michael and Holy Angels (from 1832; known as St Michael's before 1877). Wesleyan, Independent, Baptist, and Primitive Methodist congregations also recorded.
- **Record types:** Baptisms, marriages, burials, banns, confirmations (Catholic).
- **Where held:** The FamilySearch volume search (62 total digitized volumes for this place and period) found the following key indexed volumes (100% name-indexed unless noted): Holy Trinity baptisms 1841–1880 (imageGroupNumber 101149057), 1880–1898 (101149063), 1898–1910 imaged to 1900 (101149068); Christ Church baptisms 1892–1897 (101149042), 1899–1904 imaged to 1900 (101149048); St John the Evangelist baptisms 1879–1883 (101152002), 1883–1891 (101152003), 1891–1897 (101152004), 1897–1901 imaged to 1900 (101152005); Holy Trinity marriages 1871–1876 (101149084), 1876–1881 (101149089), 1881–1887 (101149094), 1887–1898 (101151995), 1898–1907 imaged to 1900 (101151996); Holy Trinity burials 1842–1983, imaged to 1900 (101151997) — 100% indexed + full-text searchable; St John marriages 1879–1894 (101152006), 1894–1900 (101152007); Christ Church marriages 1898–1904 (101149052). Catholic St Michael: baptisms 1878–1933 (imageGroupNumber 007945879_001 — browse-only), confirmations 1862–1995 and marriages 1855–1947 (imageGroupNumber 007945879_003 — 73% name-indexed). The aggregated FamilySearch collection [England, Staffordshire, Church Records, 1538–1944](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/2364451) (indexed + images) should be searched first. Also: [Staffordshire, England, Church of England Births and Baptisms, 1813–1900](https://search.ancestry.co.uk/search/db.aspx?dbid=62292) at Ancestry (subscription). For All Saints parish registers from 1875 onwards, original registers are held at the **Staffordshire Record Office** (Bishop's Transcripts run only to 1868 per the FamilySearch Catalog, koha:327194).
- **Language:** English; some Catholic records in Latin.

### Census records
- **Federal/national census:** 1881, 1891, and 1901 are fully indexed + images online. FamilySearch: [1881 England and Wales Census](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/1321821), [1891](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/1865747), [1901](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/1888129) — all free. Also at Ancestry (collections 7572, 6598, 7814) and Findmypast (subscription). FamilySearch Catalog (koha:583890): West Bromwich census returns 1841–1891 (South West and North East sub-districts) on microfilm, also available online.
- **1911 census:** [FamilySearch collection 1921547](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/1921547); Ancestry (collection 2352). Gives parents' own statement of children born alive and still living — valuable for estimating births in the 1875–1905 window.
- **Access:** All three target census years (1881, 1891, 1901) are indexed + images online at FamilySearch (free); 1911 also indexed + images.

### Probate and court records
- **Types:** Wills (testate) and administrations (intestate — for those who died without a will). Prior to 1858, probate for West Bromwich fell under the Court of the Bishop of Lichfield (Episcopal Consistory). From January 1858, the Principal Probate Registry and district registries handled English probate.
- **Where held:** National Probate Calendar (England & Wales) from 1858: indexed at [Ancestry](https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/1904) (1858–1995, subscription) and browsable at [Findmypast](http://search.findmypast.com/search-world-Records/probate-calendars-of-england-and-wales-1858-1959---browse). Original wills pre-1858 at Staffordshire Record Office / Lichfield Record Office; post-1858 wills at The National Archives.
- **Note:** Search the National Probate Calendar by surname first; it gives the date of probate, estate value, and names of executors — which can confirm relationships.

### Land records
- **Survey system:** Metes and bounds (England did not use rectangular survey).
- **Types:** Title deeds (at Staffordshire Record Office); land tax assessments 1772–1831 for West Bromwich (FamilySearch Catalog koha:410643 — available at FamilySearch Centers/Affiliate Libraries; predates the survey period).
- **Where held:** Staffordshire Record Office for historical deeds; Land Registry for modern registered titles.

### Military records
- **Relevant conflicts:** Second Boer War 1899–1902.
- **Record types:** British Army Service Records 1760–1915 at Findmypast (subscription) and Fold3; Chelsea Pensioners' Service Records 1760–1913 at [FamilySearch](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/1952868) (indexed + images, free); UK Coal Mining Accidents and Deaths Index 1878–1951 at [Ancestry](https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/62506/) (subscription).
- **Where held:** The National Archives; FamilySearch; Findmypast.

### Cemetery records
- **Major cemeteries:** Heath Lane Cemetery — burial registers 1859–1905 transcribed and indexed by [FreeReg](http://www.freereg.org.uk/parishes/sts/frontpage.shtml) (free). Holy Trinity church burials 1842–1983 are 100% indexed + full-text searchable at FamilySearch (imageGroupNumber 101151997, imaged to 1900).
- **Online coverage:** Mayers Green Congregational Church record of tombstones on FamilySearch Catalog (koha:628392); [Staffordshire Monumental Inscriptions](https://search.findmypast.com/search-world-Records/staffordshire-monumental-inscriptions) at Findmypast (subscription); [England BillionGraves Cemetery Index](http://search.findmypast.com/search-world-Records/england-billion-graves-cemetery-index) at Findmypast (subscription).
- **Physical records:** Sandwell Council holds records for Heath Lane Cemetery.

### Newspaper records
- **Local papers:** County Advertiser & Herald for Staffordshire and Worcestershire 1856–1907 at [Findmypast](https://www.findmypast.com/newspapers/england/county-advertiser-herald-for-staffordshire-and-worcestershire) (subscription); Midland Examiner and Times 1874–1877 at [Findmypast](https://www.findmypast.com/newspapers/england/midland-examiner-and-times); Staffordshire Advertiser 1795–1955 at [Findmypast](https://www.findmypast.com/newspapers/england/staffordshire-advertiser) (subscription).
- **Where held:** [British Newspaper Archive](https://www.britishnewspaperarchive.co.uk/) (subscription) has Staffordshire newspapers digitized.
- **Content value:** Obituaries, birth and marriage notices, inquests, and Poor Law notices name individuals not found in other record types.

### Immigration/emigration records
- **Relevant note:** West Bromwich is an inland industrial town. Declarations of intention and naturalizations were not a significant feature for this locally born population. However, some working-class emigration occurred in this period (Australia, Canada, USA).
- **Outgoing passengers:** [UK, Outgoing Passenger Lists, 1890–1960](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/4229516) at FamilySearch (indexed + images, free); also at Ancestry (collection 2997, subscription).
- **Content note:** Passenger lists record every person aboard including infants and young children traveling with parents. Examine the full manifest for all family members.

### Tax records
- **Types:** Land tax assessments 1772–1831 (FamilySearch Catalog koha:410643 — predates the survey period; useful background only).
- **Substitute value:** Census returns and civil registration serve as the primary substitutes for this period; no significant tax series covers 1875–1905 at the county level in the tool results.

### Other record types
- **School records:** West Bromwich school records 1892–1909 (olib:2744917) and Trinity C.E. School 1909–1914 (olib:2744918) are both online at FamilySearch. National School Admission Registers and Log-Books 1870–1914 at [Findmypast](https://search.findmypast.com/search-world-records/national-school-admission-registers-and-log-books-1870-1914) (subscription).
- **Poor Law records:** West Bromwich Poor Law Union 1834–1930. Physical records at Staffordshire Record Office. Background at workhouses.org.uk.
- **Chapter Act Books (Diocese of Lichfield) 1384–1931:** Available online at FamilySearch (koha:673554); covers church administration including 1876–1883 and 1883–1896 volumes.

## Repository guide

### Online repositories
| Repository | Collections for this place | Access |
|---|---|---|
| FamilySearch | England and Wales Birth/Marriage/Death Registration Index 1837–2008 (cols. 2285338, 2285732, 2285341); 1881/1891/1901/1911 census (cols. 1321821, 1865747, 1888129, 1921547); England, Staffordshire, Church Records 1538–1944 (col. 2364451); Parish registers for Christ Church, Holy Trinity, St John, St Andrew, St Paul, St James (olib:2744911–2744916); School records 1892–1914; Chelsea Pensioners 1760–1913 (col. 1952868) | Free |
| FreeBMD | Civil registration indexes 1837–1983+ | Free |
| Staffordshire BMD | Local BMD indexes 1837–2017 | Free |
| West Midlands BMD | Local BMD indexes | Free |
| GRO (gro.gov.uk) | Civil registration index search; certificate ordering | Free index; certificates paid |
| Ancestry | 1881/1891/1901/1911 census; Civil Registration Birth/Marriage/Death Index 1837–1915 (cols. 8912, 8913, 8914); Staffordshire Church of England Births and Baptisms 1813–1900 (col. 62292); Staffordshire BMDs 1837–2017 (col. 61709); National Probate Calendar 1858–1995 (col. 1904) | Subscription |
| Findmypast | Staffordshire Baptisms 1538–1900; Staffordshire Parish Registers Browse 1538–1900; National Burial Index; Staffordshire newspapers; Probate calendars | Subscription |
| FreeReg | Heath Lane Cemetery burial registers 1859–1905; some Staffordshire parish registers | Free |

**Coverage of this survey:** 62 digitized volumes match this place and period in volume_search (summary is complete across all 62). The 50 volumes detailed above are the first page; 12 additional volumes were not individually examined. Note also that the FamilySearch collections_search tool returned only UK-level collections (scope: United Kingdom) — the primary GRO civil registration and census collections are accessed through the repositories listed above rather than through collections_search.

### Physical repositories
| Repository | Holdings | Access method |
|---|---|---|
| Staffordshire Record Office, Stafford | Parish registers for All Saints and other West Bromwich churches; Bishop's Transcripts to c.1868; land tax assessments; pre-1858 probate | In-person or online catalogue |
| The National Archives, Kew | Post-1858 wills; military records; census originals; court records | In-person; many records online |
| Lichfield Record Office | Diocese of Lichfield records; pre-1858 Bishop's Transcripts | In-person |
| General Register Office (GRO) | Civil registration certificates | Online ordering (gro.gov.uk) |
| Birmingham Archdiocesan Archives | Originals for St Michael and Holy Angels Catholic records | Contact the archives (per FamilySearch Catalog koha:762327) |

## Records NOT online

- All Saints Church (C of E, the ancient parish) parish registers for 1875–1905: the online FamilySearch volumes found in this survey do not include an All Saints baptism register for this period; verify coverage within FamilySearch collection 2364451 and, if not present, consult original registers at the Staffordshire Record Office.
- Original GRO birth, marriage, and death certificates: must be ordered from the GRO. The quarterly index entry does not give parents' names for births registered before 1911.
- West Bromwich probate records pre-1858 (under Lichfield Episcopal Consistory): physical only at Lichfield Record Office / Staffordshire Record Office.
- Land title deeds for private properties: physical at Staffordshire Record Office.
- Poor Law Union records (workhouse admission registers, settlement examinations, bastardy bonds): physical at Staffordshire Record Office.
- Nonconformist (Wesleyan, Independent, Baptist) chapel registers not yet digitized online: check FamilySearch collection 2364451, FreeReg, and Staffordshire Record Office.

## Known record losses

No tool result in this survey reported specific record losses for West Bromwich civil registration or church records in the 1875–1905 period. An empty search result is a coverage gap, not confirmed destruction. For any series not located online, the Staffordshire Record Office and Lichfield Record Office are the repositories identified by the FamilySearch Wiki and Catalog for originals.

## Research tips

1. **Civil registration is the primary source for 1875–1905 births.** The GRO index is available free at [FreeBMD](http://www.freebmd.org.uk/) and the [GRO website](https://www.gro.gov.uk/). It gives the district, quarter, year, volume, and page. Order the full birth certificate to obtain the mother's maiden name and informant — these are the keys to identifying siblings. ([England Civil Registration](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/England_Civil_Registration))
2. **Search all three target census returns systematically.** The 1881, 1891, and 1901 censuses are fully indexed + images at FamilySearch (free). Each census gives ages, birthplaces, and relationships of every household member; a child absent from one census may appear in another. Also search the 1911 census, which required mothers to state the number of children born alive and still living. ([England Online Genealogy Records](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/England_Online_Genealogy_Records))
3. **Search multiple West Bromwich churches for christenings.** There is no single parish register for the whole district. The FamilySearch collection [England, Staffordshire, Church Records, 1538–1944](https://www.familysearch.org/search/collection/2364451) aggregates many parishes and is the best starting point; supplement with [FreeReg](http://www.freereg.org.uk/) (free) and [Staffordshire Baptisms](https://search.findmypast.com/search-world-records/staffordshire-baptisms) at Findmypast (subscription). ([West Bromwich All Saints, Staffordshire, England Genealogy](https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/West_Bromwich_All_Saints,_Staffordshire,_England_Genealogy))

entry.narrative_markdown:
## Additional Children of Hannah Earnest and Edwin Grice: Proof Summary

**Research question:** What children did Hannah Earnest (born 1857, Darlaston, Staffordshire) and Edwin Grice (born circa 1854, West Bromwich, Staffordshire) have besides their five known children — John, Hannah Grace, Edwin, William, and James?

### Source classification

All five records examined are from the indexed collection "England, Staffordshire, Church Records, 1538–1944" on FamilySearch, a derivative source (transcription-based index of original Staffordshire parish registers). Each record carries primary information supplied by informants with direct knowledge: the officiating clergy recorded the christening date (informant proximity: official duty); the presenting parents — household members — supplied the child's name and parentage. The father's name appears consistently as "Edwin Grice" across all five records; the mother's name appears consistently as "Hannah" (surname not recorded in her entries). No conflicts exist between the records, and no other conflicting evidence was identified in this project.

### The new finding: Lydia Grice

An entry dated 8 August 1878 in the Holy Trinity baptism register, West Bromwich, Staffordshire, records the christening of a daughter named Lydia Grice, with her father listed as Edwin Grice and her mother as Hannah.^1 This child does not appear in the previously documented family tree. The father "Edwin Grice" was correlated with Edwin Grice (the tree's subject husband, born circa 1854, West Bromwich) at a match score of 0.749 — probable confidence — based on an exact name match and consistent family context across the records, with no conflicting data. The mother "Hannah" was correlated with Hannah Earnest (born 1857, Darlaston), the known wife, at a match score of 0.690 — also probable confidence — based on the given name and consistent family context. The christening location, Holy Trinity, West Bromwich, is consistent with the family's established residence there; the 1881 census places the household at West Bromwich (tree fact d13ac227 on Hannah Earnest, Residence, West Bromwich, Staffordshire, 1881; this tree fact carries no linked source entry in this project's research file). Lydia's baptism falls chronologically between John (born circa 1877) and Hannah Grace (born 3 April 1880), placing her as the second child in the family sequence.

Lydia's parentage and christening are already encoded in the project tree: Edwin Grice and Hannah Earnest are linked to Lydia Grice (tree person I1) by ParentChild relationships R15 and R16, each sourced to the Lydia Grice baptism record (tree source S1). Her christening is recorded as fact F1 on I1.

### Confirming records for the five known children

The same exhaustive search returned four entries confirming previously known children, each with primary-quality parental information:

- *Hannah Grace Grice:* baptism 5 May 1880, born 3 April 1880, West Bromwich; father Edwin Grice, mother Hannah.^2 Father matched at 0.962 (confident); mother matched at 0.961 (confident).
- *Edwin Grice (junior):* baptism 1882, Darlaston; father Edwin Grice, mother Hannah.^3 Father matched at 0.985 (confident); mother matched at 0.988 (confident).
- *William Grice:* birth 12 July 1884, baptism 30 July 1884, West Bromwich; father Edwin Grice, mother Hannah.^4 Father matched at 0.926 (confident); mother matched at 0.934 (confident).
- *James Grice:* birth 10 October 1886, baptism 27 October 1886, West Bromwich; father Edwin Grice, mother Hannah.^5 Father matched at 0.923 (confident); mother matched at 0.903 (confident).

John Grice (born circa 1877) did not appear in this indexed collection; he is recorded in the tree on the basis of starting-tree evidence outside this project's source set.

### Search scope and unsearched avenues

The collection "England, Staffordshire, Church Records, 1538–1944" (FamilySearch collection 2364451) was searched exhaustively for the parent pair Edwin Grice and Hannah Grice, returning exactly five results with hasMore: false — complete enumeration of the indexed baptisms for this couple. No additional children beyond Lydia appeared.

Two record types remain unsearched and could reveal children not captured in the indexed church records:

1. The FamilySearch England and Wales Birth Registration Index (collection 2285338), filtered by mother's maiden name "Earnest," was not run. The broader search of that collection (surname Grice, birthplace West Bromwich, 2,122 results, top 20 examined) did not apply this specific filter and cannot confirm completeness. From 1875, civil registration was mandatory; GRO-registered births include children who died before baptism or were baptised at non-conformist chapels not indexed in the Staffordshire church collection.

2. The Ancestry 1911 England census (collection 2352, subscription required) was not accessible. This census records the mother's own statement of the number of children born alive and the number still living — the most authoritative available source for the couple's total birth count. FamilySearch's 1911 census index returned no result for the Edwin or Hannah Grice household. A search URL was generated (https://www.ancestry.com/search/collections/2352/?name=Edwin_Grice&birth=1854&birthplace=West+Bromwich%2C+Staffordshire%2C+England&spouse=Hannah_Grice) but could not be accessed without a subscription.

Because both sources could reveal additional children not found in the church records, the conclusion is assessed at the **possible** tier.

### Conclusion

The available evidence supports the possibility that Lydia Grice — baptised 8 August 1878 at Holy Trinity, West Bromwich, Staffordshire, daughter of Edwin Grice and Hannah Earnest — is an additional child of this couple not previously in the family tree. The exhaustive search of the indexed Staffordshire church records found no other unrecorded children in that collection. The conclusion cannot be raised to probable pending access to the filtered civil registration birth index and the 1911 census, both of which could independently establish whether additional births occurred.

---

^2 "England, Staffordshire, Church Records, 1538-1944", *FamilySearch* (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:QL3R-VWY9 : Fri Aug 21 19:48:15 UTC 2026), Entry for Hannah Grice and Edwin Grice, 5 May 1880.

^4 "England, Staffordshire, Church Records, 1538-1944", *FamilySearch* (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:QL3R-X2D1 : Fri Aug 21 23:07:14 UTC 2026), Entry for William Grice and Edwin Grice, 30 July 1884.

guardrail_shadow_violations.detail: person_evidence link written for new tree person(s) I1 with no prior same_person call: a brand-new identity should be scored before it is asserted (person-evidence/SKILL.md doctrine; issue #963). Score them with the project-relative form, which assembles both documents for you: `same_person({ projectPath, assertionId, treePersonId: "I1" })`. `assertionId` is the assertion the link cites. The tool resolves the record itself and builds the tree side as that person's matching mob, so you hand-build nothing (person-evidence, 'Call it with references, not documents'). If this call was denied, the entire batch was rejected — including any ops in other sections — and must be re-issued after the same_person call. A relationship or marriage assertion names two parties and gets a link for each. The call is about the assertion's own `record_role` party by default; for the OTHER party add `recordRole` (or `recordPersonaId`) naming it. Reusing the first party's persona for the second is how a near-zero score gets manufactured and then explained away. If the tool answers that the record holds no persona for that party, or that the candidate is a stub minted from the very persona you would be scoring (circular), say so in the link's `rationale` and proceed — the gap is still recorded; the rationale is the record of why, not a waiver. How the assertion was RETRIEVED is not such a case: a full-text hit, an image, a PDF and a sidecar-less search are all scorable, because the tool derives the record side from the record's own assertions when it cannot fetch a document. A locally-minted tree id is NOT such a case: it scores on document content and must be scored.
